evidence.claim: Parliament elected Shehbaz Sharif prime minister on April 11, 2022 after a no-confidence vote, and observers said military and intelligence interference had created an uneven electoral playing field.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Parliament elected Shehbaz Sharif prime minister on April 11, 2022 after a no-confidence vote, and observers said military and intelligence interference had created an uneven electoral playing field.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official country report based on contemporaneous monitoring and observer assessments.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers calendar year 2022 and the April 2022 transfer of power.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's accession and the coalition that brought him to office; the interference problem mostly predated his premiership.
contrary_evidence: The transfer occurred through the National Assembly rather than an extra-constitutional seizure of power.

evidence.claim: The 2022 report describes serious restrictions on free expression and media, serious restrictions on internet freedom, substantial interference with peaceful assembly and association, and security services operating without effective civilian oversight or control.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 report describes serious restrictions on free expression and media, serious restrictions on internet freedom, substantial interference with peaceful assembly and association, and security services operating without effective civilian oversight or control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official human-rights report with detailed subnational and national rights findings.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 conduct and conditions under Sharif's government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to the Sharif government period, but much of the coercive apparatus was inherited and partly outside his direct command.
contrary_evidence: The constitution formally protects speech, assembly, and association.

evidence.claim: Freedom House reported continued localized internet shutdowns and reports of internet throttling during country-wide PTI protests in May 2022.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House reported continued localized internet shutdowns and reports of internet throttling during country-wide PTI protests in May 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist internet-freedom monitoring with concrete incident reporting, though some episodes were denied by the PTA.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 target period, including the May protests.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The throttling occurred during Sharif's premiership, but implementation likely ran through telecom and security agencies rather than the PM personally.
contrary_evidence: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority denied some throttling reports.

evidence.claim: After the April 2022 political transition, authorities detained people for critical tweets, journalists were assaulted, detained, and harassed, and PEMRA warned media against criticising state institutions.
evidence.title: Journalists and critics continue to be targeted despite political transition in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: After the April 2022 political transition, authorities detained people for critical tweets, journalists were assaulted, detained, and harassed, and PEMRA warned media against criticising state institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent civic-space monitor with incident-level reporting and corroborating references to CPJ and other groups.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the first months of Sharif's premiership in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Describes the Sharif-government period, though some enforcement was carried out by police, FIA, and media regulators rather than the PM personally.
contrary_evidence: The same article notes the new government abandoned PMDA plans, which cuts against a purely repressive reading.

evidence.claim: CIVICUS rated civic space as repressed and reported that authorities continued to arrest and use excessive force against opposition protests, including PTI protests after the November 2022 shooting of Imran Khan.
evidence.title: Authorities in Pakistan continue harassment of journalists, persecution of activists and stifling of protests
evidence.excerpt: CIVICUS rated civic space as repressed and reported that authorities continued to arrest and use excessive force against opposition protests, including PTI protests after the November 2022 shooting of Imran Khan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent civic-space monitor summarizing multiple 2022 incidents and linking them to protest suppression.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers late 2022 under Sharif's government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to national authorities during Sharif's premiership, though some operations were conducted by provincial police and local security forces.
contrary_evidence: Opposition protests still occurred at scale, indicating space for mobilization remained open enough for mass action.

evidence.claim: The information minister announced that PMDA would be abolished and that journalist-protection and right-to-information work would be strengthened.
evidence.title: Information Minister announces disbanding of PMDA
evidence.excerpt: The information minister announced that PMDA would be abolished and that journalist-protection and right-to-information work would be strengthened.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government announcement of an actual policy reversal, though implementation still needed follow-through.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 period, shortly after Sharif took office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: A cabinet-level action under Sharif's government rather than a personal decree by Sharif, but still attributable to the administration.
contrary_evidence: This was a rollback of a proposed regulator, not proof of durable reform or of wider media freedom.

evidence.claim: PEMRA issued fresh directives warning satellite TV channels of legal action for propaganda, misinformation, and disinformation against state institutions.
evidence.title: PEMRA warns TV channels for propaganda, misinformation against state institutions
evidence.excerpt: PEMRA issued fresh directives warning satellite TV channels of legal action for propaganda, misinformation, and disinformation against state institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official regulator directive documenting an actual restraint on media speech.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Issued by a regulator operating during Sharif's premiership; attribution to Sharif is indirect because the notice came from PEMRA rather than the PM personally.
contrary_evidence: The government also issued public statements supportive of press freedom, so this is better read as mixed institutional practice than unambiguous personal censorship.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif was elected prime minister by the National Assembly with 174 votes after PTI boycotted the election and resigned from the assembly.
evidence.title: Shehbaz Sharif elected as Prime Minister
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif was elected prime minister by the National Assembly with 174 votes after PTI boycotted the election and resigned from the assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary result announced the same day as the vote.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the April 2022 succession event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's accession and the constitutional transfer that brought him into office.
contrary_evidence: The PTI boycott means the vote occurred in a polarized and incomplete parliamentary environment.

evidence.claim: After Imran Khan was shot, his supporters held nationwide protests, blocked major roads, and in some places clashed with security forces; police used tear gas in Islamabad.
evidence.title: Ex-Pakistani PM Khan supporters hold nationwide protests, demand political change
evidence.excerpt: After Imran Khan was shot, his supporters held nationwide protests, blocked major roads, and in some places clashed with security forces; police used tear gas in Islamabad.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting syndicated by Euronews, with direct contemporaneous incident coverage.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the November 2022 protest episode.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The protests and the police response occurred during Sharif's premiership, though the immediate trigger was an attack on Khan rather than an act initiated by Sharif.
contrary_evidence: Sharif publicly called for a transparent inquiry into the shooting, which cuts against a one-sided repression reading.
